title: Claude Code and Codex: strengths, trade-offs, and dated history
act: Act II — Where the field is
takeaway: Compare current provider freedom, integration depth, policy, and defaults—not obsolete missing-feature claims.

scenes.title: Start with the strengths
scenes.visual: 4.1.1: diagram presents equal-size product cards, not a winner podium; dateStamp stays visible. 4.1.2: reveal Codex license/provider label. 4.1.3: reveal Claude integration label with gradeBadge C. 4.1.4: retain both cards with local LSP setup and model/API compatibility conditions always visible.

sentences.text: Claude Code and Codex pair leading benchmark results with substantial tools, but they make different choices about openness and control.
Codex CLI is Apache-licensed and supports custom providers and local models; its cloud service has separate authentication requirements.
Claude Code documents subagents, language-server plugins, and deferred MCP loading, so missing-feature criticisms from earlier versions can mislead.
Language-server plugins need local setup, while provider compatibility depends on the selected model and API.

onScreen.text: As of 2026-10-08 · Terminal-Bench 4.0 official board: Claude Code and Codex model–agent combinations lead. These are system results, not isolated harness scores.
Codex CLI: Apache-2.0; custom/local providers. Cloud authentication and entitlements remain separate.
Claude Code: subagents; LSP plugins require plugin + server installation and exclude cloud sessions; MCP definitions deferred by default.

sentences.text: Today, Claude Code loads those definitions on demand, leaving more context available before a tool is needed.
Around that time, Pi creator Mario Zechner described frustration with changing behavior and limited visibility into the model’s context.
The design choice is when tool information enters context, not simply how many tools a harness offers.

onScreen.text: 2025-11-24 · Anthropic example: 58 tools, approximately 55K tokens before conversation, across GitHub, Slack, Sentry, Grafana and Splunk. Not a universal session measurement.
As of 2026-10-08 · MCP tool definitions deferred by default; names and server instructions still consume context before use.
Mario Zechner · 2025-11-30 creator account: changing behavior, context control, interaction visibility. Historical personal assessment.

scenes.title: Policy has separate lanes
scenes.visual: 4.4.1: diagram separates credential handling from billing, with compact label cards for restrictions and license terms. 4.4.2: timeline displays June pause and October update beside separate-credit conditions. 4.4.3: keep unmodified-client hosting conditions and unresolved interpretation caption visible; no compliance seal. Each card has its own evidence chip and dateStamp.

sentences.text: Anthropic’s credential rules bar third-party developers from collecting Claude account tokens or routing Free, Pro, or Max plan requests on behalf of their users.
Its October seventh update nevertheless says Agent SDK, noninteractive CLI, and third-party apps can still use subscription limits.
End users may sign into the unmodified Claude Code client; the pages leave some third-party authentication routes unspecified.

onScreen.text: As of 2026-10-08 · Credential lane: no third-party Claude.ai login offerings; no routing through users’ Free/Pro/Max credentials; no collecting, storing or intermediating Claude.ai credentials/session tokens. Sign-in must complete through Anthropic’s own flow.

Billing lane · 2026-06-15: SDK changes paused. 2026-10-07: Agent SDK, claude -p and third-party apps can still use subscription limits. Eligible Max/Team accounts can claim separate monthly API credits; those credits do not cover interactive Claude Code or extra usage.
As of 2026-10-08 · Separate billing and credential rules; these pages do not certify any particular third-party authentication implementation.

Hosted Claude Code: commercial terms apply unless otherwise agreed. Binary must remain unmodified; authentication methods cannot be removed, disabled or restricted. Each end user authenticates and is billed under their own agreement; hosts may not pay for, resell or intermediate that usage.
Claude Code license terms · Commercial: Team, Enterprise, API. Consumer: Free, Pro, Max. These are not an open-source license.

scenes.title: Strength and cost together
scenes.visual: 4.5.1–4.5.2: diagram reveals a continuity/observability card with strength and cost columns. 4.5.3: sandbox scope diagram encloses shell only. 4.5.4: gradeBadge A accompanies hardening card; patched advisories remain labelled historical. 4.5.5: highlight processes outside the shell enclosure.

sentences.text: Context management brings another trade-off: compaction keeps a session going, but early conversational instructions can be lost.
Claude Code shows context usage; Codex’s documented server-side compaction can retain an opaque, encrypted representation.
Execution boundaries also vary: Claude Code’s local Bash sandbox covers shell commands and defaults off.
Revised, peer-reviewed ToolLeak research found newer Claude Code configurations resisted its tested command-invocation attack after older configurations had failed.
Patched advisories show why implementation details matter; check which tools and processes actually sit inside your chosen boundary.

onScreen.text: As of 2026-10-08 · Continuity ↔ recall: compaction is not lossless. Claude Code: context inspection. Codex: documented server-side opaque encrypted compacted representation.
As of 2026-10-08 · Claude local Bash sandbox: off by default; shell commands only. File/web tools, MCP, LSP and hooks run outside it. Codex command networking defaults off.

Patched advisories: Codex CVE-2025-59532 fixed CLI 0.39.0 / extension 0.4.12 (cwd write-root flaw; network restriction not bypassed). Claude CVE-2026-25725 fixed 2.1.2 (absent settings file, malicious bubblewrap execution, restart). No victim-rate inference.

ToolLeak revised v6, 2026-06-28: Claude Code 2.1.138 tested cells: 0 successes / 10 attempts each; Sonnet 4, 4.5, 4.6, Opus 4.7. Attacker-controlled external tool, selected configurations; older 2.0.37 cells had successes. Not a causal defense ablation or population risk estimate; Codex not evaluated.

scenes.title: Accepted work is a different outcome
scenes.visual: 4.6.1: statCard and diagram form a PR funnel. 4.6.2: show revision branch and human-baseline caveat, never a product ranking. 4.6.3: hold observational caveats and revision branch together.

sentences.text: A peer-reviewed study of early Claude Code contributions found four hundred seventy-five of five hundred sixty-seven pull requests merged.
Two hundred fourteen merged requests needed revisions, and the matched human submissions also commonly changed before acceptance.
That observational sample measures contribution workflows, not today’s defect rate or a controlled contest between harnesses.

onScreen.text: TOSEM 2026 · Marked Claude Code-assisted PRs created 2025-02-24–2025-04-30: 475 / 567 merged; 214 / 475 merged PRs revised. Matched human PRs also commonly revised. Observational selection; open PRs excluded; client/model versions uncontrolled.

scenes.title: Choose the boundaries
scenes.visual: 4.7.1: diagram separates benchmark result from accepted contribution. 4.7.2: four equal question cards bridge to philosophies, without vendor ranking.

sentences.text: Passing a benchmark and delivering an accepted, maintainable contribution are different outcomes.
Choose on provider freedom, integration depth, deployment scope, and defaults, rather than yesterday’s missing-feature list.

onScreen.text: Decision questions: provider freedom · integration depth · deployment scope · out-of-box defaults.
